transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... I keep hearing this man's voice. It comes right out of the garage vents at the shop, and sometimes from under the hood of the cars I'm working on. It's as clear as you sitting right there, telling me not to trust my husband, and warning me not to touch certain cars. 

Which is a real problem because I'm a mechanic. If I don't touch the cars, I can't do my job, right? I've been working on cars since I took some classes at the community college. My instructor back then had this beautiful 1969 Mustang, but the alternator was always giving him trouble. He used to say a machine has a soul, you just have to listen to it. I bought this really nice socket set for that class, still use it today actually. Snap-on. Costs an arm and a leg, but the warranty is incredible. My husband complained about the price when I bought them, but he doesn't understand quality tools. He bought this cheap blender last week that broke on the very first try. 

Anyway, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, the man in the vents just keeps talking to me about my husband and the cars.
How long have you been hearing this man's voice?

It's been... gosh, about ten months now, I think. Both the voice and that feeling that someone is tracking me. Ten months is a long time, you know? It started right around the time the shop got that new air compressor. It's a Quincy, really powerful, but man, the vibration on that thing is something else. It rattles the whole back wall if you don't bolt it down right. I told the shop manager, I said, "Dave, you gotta put rubber mounts under those feet or it's gonna drive us all crazy." He didn't listen, of course. Dave never listens. He thinks because he wears a tie to a mechanic shop he knows better than the people turning the wrenches. He actually spilled coffee on his tie last Tuesday and tried to get it out with brake cleaner. I could have told him that would ruin the silk, but... well, he wouldn't have listened anyway. Brake cleaner is amazing for getting grease off a rotor, though. Evaporates in seconds. But yeah, ten months of this guy talking to me.

...have I felt any changes in my mood? Well, yeah, it's been a real rollercoaster, honestly. Sometimes I'll just be flying so high, like I have this incredible energy and I feel like I could fix every single car in town, no problem. Just knock 'em out one by one. But then... if my husband even just asks why the dishes aren't done, or if one of the other techs at the shop moves my socket set—that Snap-on set I was telling you about—I just absolutely blow up. I get so angry, like they're doing it on purpose just to hold me down, you know? 

Speaking of dishes, we have this dishwasher that's practically an antique. It's a Whirlpool from, like, 2005. The pump motor is starting to whine, and I know I could replace it in about an hour if I just ordered the part. But my husband insists we should just buy a new one. A new one! Do you know how much they charge for appliances these days? And they don't even make them with real metal anymore, it's all plastic tubs and cheap electronic control boards that fry the second there's a power surge. The older ones, they had these mechanical timers... you could actually hear them clicking through the cycles. Click, click, click... kind of soothing, really. But anyway, yeah, I get really irritable and just explode on people lately.
Have you heard the voice at times when your mood felt completely normal?

Yeah, actually... there was this stretch of a few weeks where things were pretty quiet for me. I was sleeping a lot more, just resting, you know? Not making all those huge plans to overhaul everything like I do when I'm really revved up. But even during that quiet time, I still heard the voice coming from the garage vents. And I still knew for a fact that my husband and my boss were tracking me. 

Speaking of my boss, Dave, he actually installed these new security cameras at the shop right around then. He claimed it was for "insurance purposes," but they're these crazy 4K high-definition dome cameras with infrared night vision. You know how infrared works, right? It picks up heat signatures. I got really into reading about thermal imaging a while back when I was trying to figure out the best way to diagnose a misfiring cylinder. Because sometimes a standard laser thermometer just doesn't cut it when you're trying to find a dead hole on an exhaust manifold. You point the laser, but if your hand shakes and you're off by even half an inch, you get a completely wrong temperature reading. So thermal imaging is way better for that. But those cameras Dave bought... totally excessive for a basic auto shop. He said he got a deal on them at Costco. Have you been to Costco on a Saturday? It's an absolute madhouse. You go in for a rotisserie chicken and you come out with a kayak and a fifty-pound bag of flour. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my mood. Yeah, even when I was feeling totally normal and just resting, the voice was definitely still there, and the tracking didn't stop.
Have you used any recreational drugs, alcohol, or medications around the time these experiences started or recently?

No, no drugs or anything like that. I don't really drink either, maybe a beer at a barbecue once in a blue moon, but that's it. I don't take any medications. Actually, wait, I did take some ibuprofen a couple weeks ago because I tweaked my shoulder. 

It was the stupidest thing, too. I was trying to break loose a lug nut on this F-250 that some guy had completely over-torqued. You know those pneumatic impact wrenches? They're great, but if someone just sits there and hammers on a lug nut with a one-inch drive gun, it basically cold-welds the thing to the stud. I had a three-foot breaker bar on it and I was basically hanging my entire body weight off the end of it, and when it finally popped loose, my shoulder just went *crunch*. It's the rotator cuff, I'm pretty sure. The supraspinatus tendon gets pinched right under the acromion if you're not careful. I read this whole article about shoulder biomechanics in mechanics, actually. It's a huge problem in the industry because you spend half your life working with your arms above your head under a lift. My uncle had to have double shoulder surgery because of it. He used to build custom hot rods out in Nevada. Beautiful cars, mostly old Fords. He had this '32 coupe... chopped top, suicide doors, the works. Painted it this unbelievable candy apple red. He mixed the paint himself.

But yeah, no drugs or anything like that. Just the ibuprofen for my shoulder.
